newsitem.title: UK: Serbian opposition urges return of exiled Prince.
newsitem.headline: Serbian opposition urges return of exiled Prince.

text.p: Serbian opposition leaders on Wednesday visited exiled Crown Prince Alexander near his London home and called for him to be installed as monarch in their republican homeland.
Vuk Draskovic of Serbia's Zajedno (Together) coalition said Alexander could play a similar role to Spain's King Juan Carlos, who smoothed its path to democracy after years of dictatorship.
Draskovic, who met the Crown Prince along with fellow Zajedno leaders Zoran Djindjic and Vesna Pesic, said all Serbia was shamed by the royal heir's continued exile.

"Serbia needs today our Serbian Juan Carlos and we have him in this city," Draskovic told reporters. "That is shame on us, all of us in Serbia, that he has still the status of a refugee, he still has no Serbian citizenship and his private property is in the hands of Communist rulers."
But Draskovic, a black-bearded nationalist whose views on the monarchy are not shared by all the coalition members, said a decision to restore it would depend on the Serbian people.
"I hope and I truly believe the wish of the people will be to restore the Kingdom of Serbia," he told reporters after the talks, adding that power would rest with the government.

The hour-long meeting took place at the exclusive Claridges hotel, where Alexander was born in 1945. The Crown Prince said they had discussed the need for international help in the fight to restore democracy and freedom of the press to Serbia.
"We spoke about the need for the West to to help, because the Serbian people are going through great economic hardship," he told a news conference.
"The issue at hand today is democracy, human rights and freedom of the media," Alexander said. "We are living in a dinosaur situation...and we need to move ahead and catch up."
Alexander, who has declared himself ready to take up the throne, said the focus for the month ahead was the push for open media.
The suite where Alexander was born was officially made Yugoslav territory for that day, since an heir to the Karadjordje throne must not be born on foreign soil.
But that same year, Yugoslavia's wartime leader Josip Broz Tito abolished the monarchy.
The Crown Prince, who has visited his homeland on three occasions, is the great-great-grandson of Queen Victoria and related to many of the crowned heads of Europe.

The Zajedno coalition leaders, fresh from the success of their three-month campaign in Belgrade against the annulment of local election results, earlier appealed to the West for support now that they have won some power in the street demonstrations.
They said that Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic was applying "internal sanctions" by withholding government funds from municipalities won by the opposition.
Speaking after talks with British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind, the three leaders said they were ready to initiate dialogue on political and electoral reforms with Milosevic.
Pesic said if the government did not respond to the offer to talk, they would call their supporters onto the streets again.
Rifkind said the British government strongly supported the process of dialogue and would urge Milosevic to respond.
